items.prompt: A legal integer SPD matrix gives a zero final pivot in a naive double Cholesky recurrence. What conclusion follows?

options.text: The public input must be invalid.
options.why: Exact SPD does not guarantee a positive rounded pivot in an ill-conditioned floating recurrence.

options.text: Adding jitter preserves exactly the same matrix.
options.why: Jitter changes the diagonal and therefore changes the supplied problem.

options.text: The input has been proved singular by exact arithmetic.
options.why: The premise describes a rounded pivot, not an exact singularity proof.

options.text: Rounded cancellation can erase a true positive pivot.
options.why: The extension uses exact rational LDL to preserve the guaranteed-SPD domain.

items.explanation: The extension uses exact rational LDL to preserve the guaranteed-SPD domain.
